card.name: Words that set up a prohibition
card.fires_on: The word right where a 'do not' restriction is being set up or implied, such as 'not exceeded', 'swallowed whole' before 'do not crush', or 'may not' in terms of use.

modes.label: Swallow whole
modes.description: 'whole' after an instruction to swallow extended-release tablets, ahead of a ban on crushing or chewing.
modes.example: • Swallow XELJANZ XR<< whole>> and intact. Do not crush, split

modes.label: Not exceeded / not chewed
modes.description: A negation or verb like 'exceeded' that closes a limit on dosing or handling.
modes.example: 2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION Tablets: May be taken with or without food, swallowed whole and<< not>> chewed, broken, or crushed.

modes.label: Legal or general negation
modes.description: 'NOT' or n't in a statement of what is not permitted or not possible.
modes.example: on this website is proprietary.YOU MANY<< NOT>> MODIFY, COPY, REPRODUCE

card.writes: It pushes toward Chinese words for prohibition such as 严禁, 不得 and 禁止, and toward 'unlikely'.
card.plain: It fires on words that mark a rule about what must not be done, like not crushing a tablet or not going over a dose.
